Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — p50/p95 and measurement windows

Hi Zoe — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. High-level answers below; attaching a draft SLA addendum and a short measurement spec for procurement. Attachments: SLO-draft-onyx-2026.pdf, measurement-spec-onyx.xlsx.

Summary commitments (hosted API, standard tier):
- p50: 60ms (measured at token-generation level, average prompt length ~60 tokens)
- p95: 320ms (measured per-request end-to-end generation for single-turn requests)

Measurement methodology we propose (short):
- Sliding 10-minute windows sampled at 1-minute cadence. For each 10-minute slice we compute p50/p95 across successful requests; we then report daily aggregates as the max of per-slice percentiles to avoid dilution from long tails outside the slice.
- Sampling: we include 100% of production traffic for Onyx; no synthetic sampling unless otherwise requested.
- Carveouts: planned maintenance windows (scheduled in console with 24h notice) and control-plane migrations are excluded.
- Priming/cache warm-up: requests that occur within 5 minutes of instance spin-up (autoscale events) are transient and are marked for separate analysis; they do not count toward SLA breaches but are provided in the evidence package.

Temporary derating proposal for your migration week (2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-12):
- Provisional p95 allowance: up to 500ms for the migration window, provided Onyx shares a migration schedule 72h in advance.
- Credits: For any day where p95 exceeds the provisional allowance due to migration-related load, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 10% of daily usage for that day (capped at one day).

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, we'll prepare a two-paragraph SLA addendum you can attach to the SOW and a short evidence checklist for procurement (logs, per-slice percentiles, KV-cache hit rates).
2) Ben, Karthik — can you confirm the feasibility of the 10-minute sliding window and the credit mechanics?

I'll follow up with the draft addendum by EOD.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference

Hi Zoe — thanks for the quick review. Confirmations below and we've attached the two files you requested (SLO-draft-onyx-2026.pdf, measurement-spec-onyx.xlsx).

1) Example calculation: Attached example table in the measurement-spec shows three 10-minute slices, per-slice p95 values, and the rule that the reported daily p95 equals the maximum per-slice p95. We'll include the table as a one-paragraph contract example to remove ambiguity.

2) Automatic crediting: Redwood can apply the migration credit automatically if both conditions are met: (a) Onyx submits the scheduled migration time via the Redwood Console (at least 72 hours prior), and (b) telemetry shows sustained elevated p95 coincident with the migration window and with a tagged migration label. When applied automatically, the credit will be posted to the next invoice; the process is auditable and the evidence packet (per-slice CSV + KV-cache stats) will be attached.

3) CSV export: Karthik confirmed exports will be available and we'll provide a daily CSV for the migration window (per-slice percentiles and request counts) by 2026-03-05.

4) Retries/backoff treatment: server-side retries (retries injected by the Redwood runtime) are recorded as separate failed attempts and included in percentiles; client-side retries that reuse the same request id are collapsed and measured as a single logical request. We'll include this language in the measurement appendix.

Next steps / actions:
- I've uploaded the SLA addendum draft to DocuSign (link: https://docusign.com/ONX-1259-sla-addendum). Please review and, if acceptable, sign by 2026-03-06 so we can align the migration carveout.
- Onyx to confirm the exact migration schedule in the Console (or reply with the approved window).

If procurement needs a redlined version, happy to take it and coordinate with Legal.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
